method: Both reviewers read every German string of the current file again: title and title.canDo, spec.situation and the new spec.deviation, the Folge (8 lines and the gist item), the three inputs (30 lines, the practice sign and the booking confirmation), the 9 exam texts, 2 strategy cards, 8 redemittel, the Sp2 task (instructions, situation, cards, aiRole, openingLine, 8 hintWords, 8 model turns), the S2 task (title, situation, taskDe, 3 Leitpunkte, checklist, model text), the 2 check lines, story beat and cliffhanger, every endLine, promptDe, option, hint and explanation.de, the rule cards rc.trennbare-verben and rc.zeitangaben-inversion (prose and tables), and the 34 u07 entries of a1.1/lexicon.json with their examples. We solved all 93 authored items blind from promptDe plus options, tiles or audio line (1 gist, 15 input, 12 structured, 33 pool, 13 reserve, 9 exam, 8 check, 2 proof) and the 8 perception items. Every sentence_building item was permuted by hand against its frame (Aussagesatz or W-Frage). For every error_correction we listed every correct correction, including every V2 order of the key's constituents. We ran 93 candidate answers through the real grader, src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js (digits, number words, 24-hour clock, „Uhr“ in and out of the blank, lower case, all V2 orders), and re-graded all 135 accepted forms of the 93 items (all correct). The exam blocks were checked against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/sd1.json (l3: 5 × richtig_falsch, signs with location, 10–25 words; h3: abc, 2 plays, 28–54 words, scaffold min 3 items in a1.1; sp2: cards-ask, 2 topics, one question and one answer per topic; s2: 3 Leitpunkte, about 30 words). Word counts were recomputed: signs 15/21/16/17/19, messages 36/31/37/33, model text 28 (32 with Anrede and Gruß). The lexical surface was walked with a script built on scripts/course-v2/lib-validate/lexicon.mjs (knownForms at a1.1-u07, licensedForms, compounds, the metalanguage allowlist) over every string of the unit, the rule cards and the lexicon examples. We checked the cast against casts/a1.json and series.json, the story against u05, u06, u08 and u12 and against a1.2-u04, and the new Dr.-Sommer scene against the plans and specs that use cast.dr-sommer (a1-2.md §5 and §17, a1.2/specs.json u05, a2.1/specs.json, b1.1/specs.json). The unit's day-by-day timeline was reconstructed (LS2 → LS3 → Thursday → u08). We read the validator rules the r1 findings depend on (ITM-01 correctionFindings, LEX-01 with metalanguage.mjs walkReadSurfaces, core-lexicon.mjs number words) and ItemView.jsx for how a hint is shown.

findings.problem: Both sentences have three movable constituents (Am Montag / ich / bis fünf; am Donnerstag / der Kurs / um elf), so they have three correct V2 orders, and the key plus one alternative covers only two. The German prompt says only „Korrigieren Sie:“; „Correct the word order.“ is in promptEn alone. A learner who fixes the planted V3 error by fronting the other time phrase writes correct German with the verb in position 2, which is exactly the rule the item trains. The real grader tells that learner it is wrong. The unit's own sentence_building items accept marked orders of the same kind (ls2-r02, ls2-p07), so the course contradicts itself on what counts as a correct order. This is the class of u04 r5-F01 (bare „Korrigieren Sie:“ rejects a correct correction, MAJOR) and of u04 r1-F04 (a correct order rejected, MAJOR). u01 r2 set the standard these items miss: „every word-order correction names „die Wortstellung“ and accepts all V2 orders“. It gets through because ITM-01's rail excuses a bare prompt when „the item accepts its alternative corrections, each with acceptedWhy“, and alternativesExplained() checks only that at least one alternative exists and each one listed is explained. It never computes which alternatives are owed. Naming „die Wortstellung“ would not help either, because the third order is also a correct word order. The other six order corrections of the unit (ls1-p10, ls1-r04, ls2-r04, ls3-p10, c07, ls2-r05) have only two movable constituents, or name the category and list every order, and are complete.

For consistency with ls2-r05 and u01, let the eight order corrections say „Korrigieren Sie die Wortstellung: …“. The longest, ls3-r04, is then 75 characters, within TXT-04. Alternatively fix position 1 in the prompt („Korrigieren Sie die Wortstellung. Beginnen Sie mit „Am Montag“.“). orders.mjs fixesFirstTile already recognises that frame, but this frame costs characters and is heavier to read.
findings.proposedRule: ITM-01 (tighten the r5-F01 rail): for an error_correction whose errorTag is an order tag (v2-inv, verb-final, connector-position, satzklammer), neither a named category nor one explained alternative is enough. accepted[] must hold every V2 order of the key's constituents, or promptDe must fix position 1. Constituents come from an optional `tiles` on the correction item (SCHEMA owner: same meaning as in sentence_building), so ITM-09's missingOrders() can run on it unchanged. An order correction with ≥ 3 movable constituents and no `tiles` is a blocker. Failing fixtures: a1.1-u07 ls2-p10 and ls3-r04. The test runs over all registered courses. The class is now in two a1.1 units (u04, u07). Count it toward §9.4 stop-the-line.

findings.problem: This sign carries the unit's Landeskunde. spec.deviation makes the plan's Fokus „Sprechzeiten einer Arztpraxis lesen“ the Anliegen of LS2–LS3, so learners read it as what a German GP's hours look like. A Hausarztpraxis that never opens in the afternoon is atypical. The usual pattern is mornings Monday to Friday, plus afternoon consultation hours on two or three days (often Mon, Tue and Thu), with Wednesday and Friday afternoons closed. A practice with a full statutory-insurance contract must also offer at least 25 consultation hours a week (§ 19a Ärzte-ZV as amended by the TSVG 2019; the fact owner verifies this before any Fact record uses it). 8–12 Monday to Friday is 20. The hours also become a series fact. Dr. Sommer is the cast's GP up to B1 (a1.2-u05, a2.1, b1.1), and a1.2-u05 plans an Ansage of an Arztpraxis on the answering machine, but the hours are recorded nowhere that those authors read.

findings.problem: The unit deliberately teaches Montag–Freitag and Wochenende and leaves Samstag and Sonntag to u08 and u11. Yet the learner meets both, and an unallocated verb, on three surfaces that the new LEX-01 walk does not read. (1) The rule-card table is German-only; the card's English twin covers the prose, not the table rows. (2) The unit's vocabulary-card examples: LEX-07 checks them against the grammar ceiling (u04 r4-F01), not against the lexis. (3) Ordinals: core-lexicon.mjs generates „erste“ … as always-known NUMBER_WORDS. knownForms() lets a later lexicon allocation outrank a core lemma, but not a generated number word, so lx.erste @ a1.2-u04 never counts, and „der erste Termin“ in the LS2 input passes unglossed. This is the u04 r2-F07 → r5-F03 class of later words on learner surfaces, on the surfaces the rail left out.
